title: Isolated function tests and contracts
goal: Build an isolated calculation test set that detects a semantic mutation.
prerequisites: onec.p2; P2: types, branching, loops and numeric boundaries.
outcomes: Build an isolated calculation test set that detects a semantic mutation.
Implement assertions and a safe summary.
sections: Before implementation, specify input, expected type, exact value and permitted changes. Include ordinary minutes, zero, an upper boundary, an omitted argument and a wrong type. Do not derive expected results by copying the same function formula: calculate small expectations independently so one defect is not reproduced in both implementation and oracle.

The service-desk calculation may be called from a card, document and report. Separate formulas let one fix leave two old implementations behind. A common computation contract avoids that divergence but needs explicit inputs. List every caller and verify equal units, parameter meaning and result type rather than merely matching function names.

A pure function needs neither a form, customer database nor current date. Each test creates its own inputs instead of depending on a previous attempt. A shared structure mutated by one case contaminates later cases. Change case order and repeat the suite. Supply clocks and external values through explicit dependencies when needed.

Describe a function by inputs, preconditions, result and permitted changes. Cost uses numeric minutes/rate, admissible ranges, a rounded number and unchanged input collections. This description selects tests before implementation. If failure returns another type, callers must know explicitly or an error can accidentally participate in arithmetic. A stable contract makes substitution and review possible.

A suite that passes correct code has not yet demonstrated sensitivity. In a separate copy, replace addition with subtraction or remove a range check. The program may still compile, but a specific case must fail. Preserve source, mutant, hashes and both summaries; never corrupt the accepted source merely for a demonstration.

Checking mutation needs more than comparing variable names:two variables can refer to one collection. Snapshot important fields and nested elements before execution, then compare the source afterwards. Run another function on the same input to expose hidden contamination. Keep each test’s setup independent so changing test order cannot alter the outcome.

PASS means named assertions held on the recorded version and input set. It does not prove learner authorship, absence of all defects or client-server behavior. Separate syntax checking, actual execution and assertion outcomes. Incomplete output, timeout or unavailable licensing are distinct states, not zero errors and not success.

A semantic negative control differs from a syntax error. Replacing addition with subtraction may compile but must change a named assertion’s result. Keep compilation and executed assertions as separate outcomes. Unavailable platforms, timeouts and incomplete case lists cannot confirm missing results. Preserve original and mutated source hashes and identify the particular assertion that detects the defect.

lab.title: Build an isolated calculation test set that detects a semantic mutation.
lab.environment: Official 1C 8.3.27.x, separate file training infobase, thick managed client; common modules are checked in their declared contexts. Record each native run separately.
steps: Create a separate work copy; record its ID, source ID and platform/configuration build. Never restore over your source.
Run ordinary, zero and boundary inputs.
Change the formula only in a separate mutant.
Reopen the copy, repeat the checks and reconcile the unchanged source. Preserve failures separately from the corrected attempt.

mistakes: Treat an expected value as an observed execution.
